cells.tense: What you made is moving between people now, and it comes back to you evenly.
cells.act: set the finished thing down in a form that keeps
cells.ask: Pick one arrangement you already have with somebody close — how money moves, how the favors go — and set its shape on one page, enough that it would stand if you weren't there to run it.
cells.core:
The harvest arrived and it's out in the open now. What you worked out for yourself about giving and taking is running through the people near you, and roughly as much comes back as goes out. Standing back, you can see the whole arrangement, and the shape of it is level. That is rarer than it sounds, and it isn't luck.

The next piece is holding it. On the tired days, the distracted days, the stretches you're away from all of them, propping the thing up by hand is the cost. Put its shape on paper once — who does what, how it splits — and part of that stops depending on you being there to do it. One page, kept where you'll find it.

cells.tense: You will keep a close watch on who has given what, and the watch will cost you the exchange itself.
cells.act: persist on your own reserves through the pressure
cells.ask: For the coming week, stop tracking whether your share and theirs come out even. Handle what is plainly yours, alone, and leave their portion to them until Sunday.
cells.core:
From where you stand you can see every portion at once. Who gave last time, who's behind now, who hasn't matched what they took — and the watching feels like what keeps things honest. It has started shaping the arrangement instead of describing it. Bracing for a debt that hasn't arrived is more tiring than the debt would be.

What steadies this is your own footing, not a tighter grip. Take your portion for the coming week, all of it, on your own reserves, and let the other portions settle where they settle. Not coldly — just your part, done, with nothing else in your hands. By Sunday you'll know whether the count you've been running was holding anything up.
cells.sheetLine: Where you can see everything, the counting becomes the work.
cells.verb: To give and receive in equal measure

cells.tense: The exchange happened around you, and you were standing at the door while it did.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Look at how you spent yourself this past week: what actually landed somewhere, and what just drained. Pick one entry from the draining side and drop it from the week ahead.
cells.core:
You put in, and the shape of it stayed on your side of the table. Nothing came back with your name attached, and by now the pattern is steady enough that you can see the whole of it. The arrangement looks fine from any angle. Your own place in it is the part that went quiet.

What sharpens is your eye, not the exchange. Go through last week and separate what reached somebody from what asked and got nothing. That distinction is the entire work, and it needs no one's help. Drop the entry you least want to keep. Something will come back your way, and it'll be yours rather than owed.

cells.tense: The evening-out in this room has a keeper, and the keeper would say the room simply works.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Before the next quiet adjustment — covering a gap, stepping back so another gets the credit — wait a beat and know that it's you making it. Then act, or leave it. Both are allowed.
cells.core:
In this harvest, things come level. A shortfall gets covered, a win gets handed to someone else, and the books come right — and if anybody asked, you'd say the people here are simply decent to one another. That's true. What's also true is that the leveling has a hand behind it, and the hand belongs to you.

Seeing it isn't the same as claiming credit. Hold both facts at once: the room works, and you're part of why. Wait a beat before the next quiet correction, long enough for the move to be yours in your own knowledge, then make it or don't. The difference is only whether you were standing beside it.
cells.sheetLine: The balance here is yours. Your word for it is chemistry.

attempts.check: The record supports the mechanism and the acts but not what any specific person is doing with the fairness — whether they run the ledger, have stopped, or never noticed their own hand in it. A reader could fairly say 'I don't keep score at all, people just seem to even things out around me,' and the Too Much cell would be describing a stranger. The asks all survive that: nothing in them depends on the ledger being real, and each teaches something about the person's own giving whether my read lands or not. The sentence that serves me more than them is the one about arriving at the harvest with nothing to show for it — it flatters the mechanism by giving the person a sad ending they never reported.
